title: Security Operations suite: Exposure Management, Threat Management, Red Canary MDR, managed threat hunting and CTEM

prose.text: {{exposure-components}} The Data Fabric page lists a different set {{divergence:exposure-portfolio-members}}. {{ctem-program}} {{uvm-ctem}}

Whether CTEM stages map onto the suite's products is open {{gap:ctem-stages}}. Whether customers buy CTEM as a bundle is open {{gap:ctem-bundle}}. Whether CTEM has an SDK of its own is open {{gap:ctem-sdk}}.
The product entries are [[aem.overview]], [[uvm.overview]], [[risk360.overview]] and [[easm.findings]]; the shared data layer is in [[aem.secops-platform]].

Whether managed threat hunting targets TTPs that automated detection misses is open {{gap:mth-scope}}. Whether it is the human-expertise component within Red Canary MDR is open {{gap:mth-within-mdr}}. Whether it is delivered only as a managed service through the account team is open {{gap:mth-delivery}}.
Integration with the rest of the suite is open {{gap:red-canary-integration}}, and so is any customer SDK or delivery model {{gap:red-canary-delivery}}.

Identity Protection, SOC Workbench and Breach Predictor are in [[identity-protection.overview]], [[soc-workbench.overview]] and [[breach-predictor.overview]]. The AI-automation layer is described in [[portfolio.platform]].

checks.do: For a question about which SecOps product fits a need, route to that product's overview and answer from its claims; the suite page only groups the products.
For Red Canary delivery or integration questions, say the answer is open and do not infer an SDK, portal or account process.
For CTEM stage mapping, say the mapping is open and do not assign suite products to CTEM stages.

suite-brand.statement: The Security Operations page calls the suite the unifying brand for Zscaler's Exposure Management and Threat Management offerings.

quotes: This is the unifying brand for Zscaler's Exposure Management + Threat Management offerings.

exposure-components.statement: The Exposure Management components the page lists are Asset Exposure Management, Unified Vulnerability Management, Risk360 (risk quantification across Zscaler systems with configuration-change recommendations) and CTEM.

quotes: Asset Exposure Management (AEM)
Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM)
**Risk360** — risk quantification across Zscaler systems with configuration-change recommendations
Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM)

ctem-program.statement: CTEM is marketed as a scalable program spanning assets, data, identity, cloud and SaaS.

quotes: scalable program spanning assets, data, identity, cloud, SaaS

uvm-ctem.statement: The UVM marketing page positions UVM as a CTEM accelerator, which it spells Continuous Threat and Exposure Management.

quotes: Positioned as a Continuous Threat and Exposure Management (CTEM) accelerator

easm-component.statement: EASM is positioned as a component of the broader Security Operations and Exposure Management portfolio rather than a standalone product page.

quotes: EASM is positioned as a component of the broader Security Operations / Exposure Management portfolio rather than a standalone product page.

threat-components.statement: The Threat Management entries the page lists are Deception Technology, Red Canary Managed Detection & Response (MDR) and Managed Threat Hunting.

quotes: Deception Technology
Red Canary Managed Detection & Response (MDR)
Managed Threat Hunting

mth-hunting.statement: Managed Threat Hunting is described as expert-led 24×7 hunting for sophisticated threats and anomalies.

quotes: **Managed Threat Hunting** — expert-led 24×7 hunting for sophisticated threats and anomalies
expert-led 24×7 hunting for sophisticated threats and anomalies

red-canary-status.statement: Red Canary MDR operates initially as a separate business unit within Zscaler and functions as an AI-powered augmentation for SOC teams.

quotes: Operates initially as a separate business unit within Zscaler
Red Canary MDR functions as an AI-powered augmentation for SOC teams

red-canary-combined.statement: The page says Red Canary MDR is combined with Zscaler's data and ThreatLabz intelligence to deliver an agentic SOC that combines AI-driven workflows with human expertise.

quotes: Red Canary MDR functions as an AI-powered augmentation for SOC teams
Combined with Zscaler's high-quality data + ThreatLabz intelligence to deliver an "agentic SOC"
combining AI-driven workflows with human expertise

red-canary-metrics.statement: Zscaler's marketing cites 10× faster threat identification and a 99.7% threat accuracy rating for the suite.

quotes: Threats identified and stopped **10× faster**
**99.7% threat accuracy** rating

ctem-stages.title: How the five CTEM stages map onto the suite's products
ctem-stages.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'The five-stage CTEM model (scoping, discovery, prioritization, validation, mobilization) maps onto Zscaler's suite roughly as: AEM scopes and discovers, UVM prioritizes, Deception validates, Risk360 reports up.' No captured page gives a five-stage CTEM model or this mapping.

ctem-bundle.title: Whether customers buy CTEM as a multi-product bundle
ctem-bundle.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Customers buy the program (typically as a multi-product bundle within Security Operations) rather than a single discrete offering.' No captured page describes how CTEM is purchased.

mth-within-mdr.title: Whether Managed Threat Hunting sits inside Red Canary MDR
mth-within-mdr.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Managed Threat Hunting is distinct from but complementary to Red Canary MDR (Red Canary is the broader MDR layer; MTH is the specialized human-expertise component within it).' The suite page lists Red Canary MDR and Managed Threat Hunting as separate entries and does not nest one in the other.

mth-scope.title: Whether managed threat hunting targets TTPs that automated detection misses
mth-scope.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Proactive search for sophisticated threats, anomalies, and TTPs that automated detection misses.' The suite page says expert-led 24×7 hunting for sophisticated threats and anomalies, and nothing about TTPs or automated detection gaps.

mth-delivery.title: How managed threat hunting is delivered and engaged
mth-delivery.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Pure managed-service delivery: no portal configuration surface, no SDK; customer engagement is via the Zscaler account team.' The suite page describes a 24×7 expert-led service and no engagement path.

red-canary-integration.title: How Red Canary MDR integrates with the rest of the suite
red-canary-integration.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Integration semantics with the rest of the SecOps suite are still emerging at capture date; Red Canary's standalone product surfaces remain operational.' The suite page says only that Red Canary operates initially as a separate business unit, and gives no integration semantics or current status.

red-canary-delivery.title: Whether Red Canary MDR has a customer SDK or portal surface
red-canary-delivery.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'No customer SDK surfaced specifically for Red Canary; managed-service-shaped delivery.' A search of the vendored code found no Red Canary mention; the captured pages describe it as a service and name no interface.

ctem-sdk.title: Whether CTEM has an SDK surface of its own
ctem-sdk.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'No SDK — program-level offering; the SDK surfaces of the underlying products are what's accessible.' The suite capture describes CTEM as a program and names no API or SDK for it; the underlying products' surfaces are in their own subjects.

exposure-portfolio-members.summary: Which products make up Zscaler's Exposure Management portfolio.

quotes: Asset Exposure Management (AEM)
Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM)
Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM)

positions.says: Asset Exposure Management, Unified Vulnerability Management, Risk360 and CTEM; EASM is not listed.

quotes: forms the data aggregation backbone for the Exposure Management portfolio, which includes EASM, Risk360, and Unified Vulnerability Management.

positions.says: EASM, Risk360 and Unified Vulnerability Management; AEM and CTEM are not listed.

exposure-portfolio-members.impact: Neither page says its list is complete. An answer that names one page's list as the portfolio drops AEM or EASM; name both sources when listing the members.
